clue.text: Changes tons, as Tim Farron gets involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled up together, so these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician, Tim Farron, being drawn into a sweeping series of changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Farron was leader of the Liberal Democrats; his name simply supplies letters for the anagram signalled by 'gets involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a transformation is a thorough change, so the plural works for the plural noun.

clue.text: Helping with inside story on baseless rich

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: a scoop is an exclusive news story from inside knowledge

indicators.note: a down entry's base is its last letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: rich food is full, as in full-flavoured

explanation.surface: A tabloid offers help with a secret story about the vulgar rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping of food is a serving, and a scoopful is one such portion.

clue.text: Stop wife getting kiss off cheat

indicators.note: the kiss comes off, meaning it is removed from the word

parts.note: a hoax is a trick or deception
X is the written sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A wife breaks off a kiss with a cheating partner and calls a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection used to tell a horse, or anyone, to halt: a cry of stop.

clue.text: Horrible German to be sorry? A little

parts.note: to rue is to regret or be sorry
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: Is a German horrible to be just a little bit sorry?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something gruesome is ghastly and repellent.

clue.text: Trick shot pottable?

parts.note: lead shot is small pellets of lead
in snooker a ball that may legally be potted is said to be on

explanation.surface: A snooker player asks whether a trick shot can be potted.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a ball you are allowed to pot next is 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to lead someone on is to deceive or fool them.

clue.text: Finish urge — that woman will

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
she'll is short for she will

explanation.surface: A woman promises she will complete the task she is pushed into.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: eggshell is a paint finish with a slight sheen.

clue.text: Make fast? On the contrary (one local runner)

parts.note: 'un is a regional, dialect form of one
Usain Bolt is the famous sprinter

explanation.surface: A local runner who, far from speeding up, seems to be slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' tempts one to think of speed; here fast means secure, and the opposite of fastening a door is to unbolt it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite: to fasten a door with a bolt is to make it fast, so drawing the bolt reverses that.

clue.text: Screwing pig — Cameron hater is one making film

indicators.note: screwing up words twists them, so these letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe at David Cameron and a notorious pig story, voiced by someone who hates him.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the director of photography is the person shooting a film.

clue.text: "Being in sport is exciting" (Shearer and co)

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A football pundit like Alan Shearer and friends say being involved in sport is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England striker turned pundit; his name is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a horse bred for racing is a living creature whose life is sport.

clue.text: Spirits (rum, gin): finishes off Bacardi and coke

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so these letters are rearranged
the finishes of the words are their last letters

explanation.surface: A list of spirit drinks at a bar: rum, gin, Bacardi and coke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' and 'rum' both pose as drinks; rum is the anagram signal, mixing GIN with the last letters I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of genie: supernatural spirits of Arabian folklore.

clue.text: Baby alone on a teat's content

indicators.note: the content of the phrase is what it holds within it, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: An infant left alone, happily feeding on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: a newborn infant in its first weeks of life.

clue.text: Arrange good-looking person, ignoring hot model

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to pose is to model for a picture

explanation.surface: A photographer arranges a handsome model, ignoring the hot one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dispose things is to set them out in order.

clue.text: Sporting people provided nothing to entertain

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sweet FA is slang for nothing at all
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Sports officials are happy to put on a show, provided it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The world governing body of football is an organisation of sporting officials.

clue.text: One with leaves in teapot is stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes things round, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone stirring a teapot with tea leaves inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests tea leaves; it means a plant's foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Christmas plant with red leaves is a plant, one with leaves.

clue.text: Setback as English, with less colour, return to grab sun

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold of something, so the sun's letter goes inside
return means go back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: paler means having less colour

explanation.surface: A pale English holidaymaker goes back to catch some sun after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns E + PALER into RELAPE; S then goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a relapse is a falling back into illness, a setback.

clue.text: Don't look as often outstanding

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
with 'Don't', not looking as often means looking less

explanation.surface: Advice not to stare so often when something is outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't ... as often' together mean less: peer less is to look less often.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something without equal is unrivalled and outstanding.

clue.text: Stake to run out, money invested as capital

parts.note: a pale is a wooden stake, as in a fence

indicators.note: invested money is put in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A gambler's stake is gone, money invested as capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Sicilian city is the capital of Sicily.

clue.text: Die in a film that's released

indicators.note: in signals that the film is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: per means a, as in 'once per day'
ET is the Spielberg film
out means released, as from prison

explanation.surface: A character dies in a film that has just come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to peter out is to dwindle and die away.

clue.text: See 20
Cut Beeb: air a TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An order to trim a BBC programme before it goes out on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to abbreviate is to shorten, to cut down.

clue.text: Labour hope Corbyn, a red, is excellent

indicators.note: to labour is to toil over, working these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A Labour hopeful hails Jeremy Corbyn, a left-winger, as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is the verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being above any criticism means being faultless, excellent.

clue.text: Screw with it and climax

parts.note: in means fashionable, with it
to come is slang for to reach a climax

explanation.surface: A smutty instruction about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' here is slang for wages or salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a screw is one's pay, money earned.

clue.text: Fight in bar

definitions.meaning: a pole or rod, as in a ship's mast

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: sparring is practice boxing, and a spar is a pole on a boat.

clue.text: Perfect year turning bad: papers (Conservative press)

indicators.note: the outer pieces press in on the middle, squeezing it between them

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: turning round makes the letters run backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A perfect year goes sour as the Tory press turns on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' sends the word for bad backwards; 'press' has the papers and Conservative squeeze the year and that reversal between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an idyllic scene is blissful and perfect.

clue.text: Soldiers come of age, miss women, then get back together

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: to miss something is to leave it out

parts.note: to grow up is to come of age

explanation.surface: Troops reach adulthood, miss their women, then reunite.
explanation.walkthrough: GROW UP loses W to give GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to regroup is to reassemble after being scattered.

clue.text: Name backing European exit

indicators.note: in a down clue backing means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tag is a label or name

explanation.surface: A politician names the European exit he backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gate is an opening, a way out.

clue.text: BA knocked out from "Crazy fools"

indicators.note: knocked out from means removed from the word

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An airline, BA, is shut out by crazy fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: nanas are silly people, fools.

clue.text: Whiskers around animal, hard biting its prey

indicators.note: biting holds something in the mouth, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a mouse is a cat's prey

indicators.note: around means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a cat is an animal
H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencils

explanation.surface: A cat's whiskers encircle its mouth as it bites its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its prey' is the cat's prey; 'around' turns the animal backwards, and with hard it is bitten by the prey's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair on the upper lip is often called whiskers.
